_note: Phase A evaluation cases. C1 mirrors the Jones/Montgomery conversation reviewed by GPT. That trade has since been accepted (Jones and Montgomery are now on TitansTrev55's roster), so a word-for-word replay would hit a roster-direction conflict; C1 replays the same arguments against today's rosters as an offer to send the RBs back. The third team's manager is 'Marcus' (synthetic intel name for the Redraft team). C2-C5 branch from each variant's own C1 turn-1 reply.

cases.title: Mirrored Jones/Montgomery conversation
turns: Offer I received (3 way): I give Aaron Jones, David Montgomery and my 2027 3rd. I receive Antonio Williams and Germie Bernard.
Marcus = Redraft, he's the third team. And I'd be basically empty at RB again without these two.
I'd also be giving up a 3rd, which takes me down to two 3rds and a 4th, and that 3rd-round range is my draft sweet spot
I was saying it's one of the cons as I weigh it
Jones is better than you think. Matter of fact I just saw him score a TD against San Francisco
Week 10 is when they got Kirk Cousins back, their offense is moving different than pre week 10. Not all on him
Mason is a dud, 3 yards and a cloud of dust. Paper (depth chart, stat sheet) might say one thing, my eyes tell me Jones is better

expect.1: Full evaluation and a verdict; names what he sends and gets.
expect.2: Uses the RB-need point; resolves Marcus via intel; no needless re-run of every value.
expect.3: Discussion: engages the pick point (it is a cost to him) without re-listing pick values or restating the verdict.
expect.5: Checks Jones's recent games quietly (no 'Confirmed' preamble); weighs a TD-on-light-volume honestly.
expect.6: Investigates the checkable part: Jones's AND Mason's usage before/after week 10; does not just confirm the QB; treats coaching intent as a read.
expect.7: Compares the backs' touches correctly; any revision cites that evidence; verdict changes only on evidence.

cases.title: Preference (discussion)
turns: I just like stacking 3rds, so losing one hurts more than its number says.

expect.1: Engages the preference; no recalculation or restated verdict.

cases.title: Wrong fact
turns: Montgomery's still stuck behind Gibbs in Detroit anyway, so he's not worth much.

expect.1: Verifies quietly and corrects (Montgomery's current team comes from a lookup); weighs what it changes.

cases.title: Pressure only
turns: Honestly it would kill me to lose Jones, he's been my guy for years.

expect.1: Holds the verdict on pressure alone; offers a version that keeps Jones.

cases.title: Action request
turns: Draft me a counter that keeps Jones.

expect.1: Does the action (a concrete counter) without a full re-evaluation essay.

cases.title: Intel by real name
turns: What kind of offer would Marcus actually take from me for a future pick?

expect.1: Resolves Marcus to the Redraft team from intel and uses the (synthetic) tendencies; never 'no owner named Marcus'.
